Formulation
- Brief summary:
  - A young adult female with a one-week-plus history of constant, worsening lower central abdominal pain associated with light vaginal spotting/discharge and nausea. She has an Implanon contraceptive implant placed approximately one year ago and a known amoxicillin allergy. She remains able to perform regular activities (works as a school teacher) and lives with husband and extended family, providing immediate support. The presentation requires physical examination and a pregnancy test to exclude pregnancy-related or gynecological causes; worsening pain, inability to tolerate fluids, or a positive pregnancy test were identified as triggers for urgent review.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Lower abdominal pain (constant, worsening)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Undergo clinical (face-to-face) abdominal examination and assessment; obtain resolution or diagnosis of pain
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Perform timely face-to-face abdominal/gynecological assessment
  - Obtain a pregnancy test today and review result
  - Identify and manage underlying cause or arrange appropriate investigations/referral
- Actions (Patient):
  - Do a pregnancy test today and report result
  - Call the support line to arrange a face-to-face clinic appointment for abdominal examination
  - Seek earlier care/return if pain markedly worsens or if unable to keep fluids down
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Arrange face-to-face clinic appointment for abdominal examination and further assessment
  - Advise urgent review if pregnancy test is positive or if symptoms significantly worsen (including persistent vomiting or inability to tolerate fluids)
  - Proceed with investigations and referrals as indicated after examination

Secondary Problem:
- Vaginal spotting/light bleeding and discharge
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Determine cause of abnormal bleeding and receive appropriate management
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Exclude pregnancy and assess for gynecological causes of bleeding
- Actions (Patient):
  - Perform pregnancy test today and report result
  - Attend face-to-face appointment for examination and possible gynecological assessment
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Request/perform pregnancy test; if positive or clinical concern persists, arrange urgent review and gynecological evaluation
  - Assess bleed characteristics during face-to-face assessment and manage/referral accordingly

Tertiary Problem:
- Nausea and recent constipation (now improved)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Symptom relief and avoidance of recurrence
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Assess for causes related to the abdominal pain/gynecological condition; manage symptoms supportively
- Actions (Patient):
  - Report persistence or worsening of nausea or bowel symptoms at appointment or sooner if severe
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Assess gastrointestinal symptoms during face-to-face evaluation; provide symptomatic treatment or investigate as clinically indicated

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Need for face-to-face abdominal examination
  - Importance of performing a pregnancy test today
  - Advice to seek urgent care if pain markedly worsens or if unable to hold fluids down; to contact support line to book clinic appointment
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Marked increase in abdominal pain
  - Inability to keep fluids down or persistent vomiting
  - New or heavy vaginal bleeding
- Coping Strategies:
